Consult Summary:
- Telemedicine visit for acute continuous vertigo with tinnitus and nausea beginning ~2 hours prior; prior brief similar episode 1 month ago; clinician impression: labyrinthitis; symptomatic medication prescribed and urgent in-person evaluation arranged with safety-net instructions provided.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Acute dizziness/vertigo described as room-spinning; associated nausea, unsteady gait, and bilateral ear “buzzing” (tinnitus).
- Onset/duration: Sudden onset while making breakfast ~2 hours before consult; persistent since onset. Similar episode ~1 month ago lasting 5–10 minutes and resolved spontaneously.
- Course: Current episode ongoing without relief.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors: Not discussed.
- Associated symptoms:
  - Positive: Nausea (no vomiting), unsteady gait due to vertigo, tinnitus.
  - Negative: No limb weakness, no hearing loss (hearing intact), no ear pain, no ear discharge, no recent viral illness (no cold/cough), no subjective fever.
- Systems review (pertinent negatives): As above; no additional ROS documented.

Past Medical History:
- Premature ovarian failure; on hormone replacement therapy (HRT). Associated medication: HRT (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- No other chronic medical or surgical history reported.
- Allergies: No known drug allergies.

Social History:
- Not discussed (tobacco, alcohol, drugs, occupation, living situation not documented).

Family History:
- Not discussed.

Physical Examination:
- No vitals recorded.
- No physical examination performed (telemedicine).

Investigations:
- None performed during this visit.
- Planned: In-person assessment to include otoscopic ear exam, blood pressure check, and gait/neurologic assessment.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Acute continuous vertigo with tinnitus; clinician impression: labyrinthitis.
  - Start symptomatic medication: name not documented, prescribed as “1 tablet three times daily,” 10-day supply; can be taken with or without food. (Medication name and dose/route not documented.)
  - E-prescription sent to Lloyds Pharmacy (per system record).
  - Arrange urgent in-person clinical assessment to examine ears, check blood pressure, and assess gait/neurologic status.
  - Safety-net: Seek emergency care (A&E/ED) if new limb weakness, sudden severe headache, or persistent violent vomiting develops.
  - Patient advised to contact support to book the appointment.
- Issue 2: Nausea associated with vertigo.
  - Addressed with above symptomatic management. No current vomiting reported. Monitor; escalate if vomiting becomes persistent/violent.
- Issue 3: Premature ovarian failure on HRT.
  - Chronic condition noted; no changes to HRT discussed during this visit.

General plan items:
- Follow-up: In-person evaluation within the next few days as arranged; reassess diagnosis and management after examination.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: Vitals, full neurologic exam (including nystagmus, cerebellar testing), orthostatic vitals, otoscopic findings, comprehensive medication reconciliation (HRT details), pregnancy status, detailed social history, and family history.
- Internal conflicts: Patient reported “premature ovarian failure,” while clinician verbally repeated “premature hearing failure” (conflict noted).
- Transcript quality: Minor audio dropouts; medication name not captured; otherwise understandable.
